result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.bfs_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get the edges a breadth-first search follows. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.bfs_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get the edges a breadth-first search follows. title: >- [Graph.bfs_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the edges a breadth-first search follows. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the edges a breadth-first search follows. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L54910-L54986){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.bfs_edges( source, depth_limit=None, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![BFS edges](../assets/graphs/bfs-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A triangle A, B, C with a tail C to D, searched breadth-first from A (outlined). The tree edges are numbered in discovery order: A finds both B and C before moving on, so C is reached directly from A and the edge B-C is not used; the separate pair E-F is never reached. The card lists (A, B), (A, C), (C, D)." width="100%"} A breadth-first search explores the graph in rings around `source=`: first every neighbor, then every neighbor's unvisited neighbors, and so on. Each newly reached node is discovered along exactly one edge, from the node that found it. Those edges, in discovery order, form the BFS tree, and following them from the source gives a fewest-hops path to every reachable node. `bfs()` returns only the visit order; this returns the tree itself, which tells you *how* each node was reached. Neighbors are explored in edge insertion order, the same order `bfs()` uses, so the children of each edge appear in `bfs()` order. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. [depth_limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop expanding at this many hops from the source. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default) follows them forward, `"in"` backward, and `"all"` in both directions. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(parent, child)` node-ID pairs in the order the children were discovered. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist, `depth_limit=` is negative, or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a triangle with a tail, C is reached directly from A, not through B, because BFS looks at all of A's neighbors before moving on: ::: {#23e55fd7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) label = graph.get_label_from_id [(label(p), label(c)) for p, c in graph.bfs_edges("A")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('A', 'C'), ('C', 'D')] ``` ::: :::
